title: ANZ migrates 1.7 petabytes of data to AWS
html:
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (ANZ) has completed a cloud migration effort to Amazon Web Services (AWS).

The company revealed earlier this week that it has migrated one of its largest data platforms to AWS, in total moving some 1.7 petabytes of data.

The migration was completed in six months, despite estimates expecting it to take 18 months, with the use of AI-assisted engineering to help with analyzing, converting, testing, and optimizing workloads. The bank said that engineers used a troubleshooting AI assistant powered by Amazon Bedrock to identify and fix performance bottlenecks using the chatbot, without needing to manually comb through code and configurations.

The new platform is hope to provide greater scalability and resilience to ANZ and enable the bank to improve customer and employee experience.

ANZ chief data and AI officer, Kai Yang, said: "Data is the foundation of modern banking and increasingly the foundation of AI. As we explore new ways to use data and analytics to improve customer and employee experiences, having modern, scalable and secure infrastructure is critical. This transformation modernizes one of ANZ's most important data platforms and provides a stronger foundation for future innovation. It gives us greater flexibility to scale and simplify our technology environment and accelerate the development of new data and capabilities over time."

AWS managing director for Australia and New Zealand, Chris Casey added: "Migrating a major banking data platform while it continues to serve customers in real time is one of the most complex undertakings in financial services. Completing a migration of this scale in six months reflects the trust and world-class delivery capability of AWS Professional Services, AWS Partners, and the team at ANZ."

ANZ is a known customer of IBM's mainframes, and according to an A.G.Coombs case study, has two data center facilities in Melbourne, Australia. In 2009, a 4,000 sqm (43,055 sq ft) data center was also listed in Highbrook, Auckland.

In its 2026 Annual Report, the bank noted that its technology expenses had decreased by $186 million (eight percent), which was "driven by ongoing technology simplification and lower amortization from change in useful lives of select strategic software assets, partially offset by inflationary impacts on vendor costs."

In 2025, AWS said it would invest $13bn in expanding its data center infrastructure in Australia.

Australia's CommBank and Westpac have both migrated significant workloads and data to the cloud provider.
summary: Aussie multinational bank completes migration to AWS
